_comment: Step 17C discriminating retrieval benchmark. Frozen BEFORE any retrieval was run or any result reviewed. Every query is grounded in a real, inspected item from the live 93-item dev corpus (see evaluation/step17c-corpus-snapshot.md) — 'expectedRationale' is Claude's own defensible-relevance note, written before seeing retrieval output, NOT shown to the human judge and NOT used to auto-grade anything. Categories: exact (repo/title/entity), literal_keyword (a rare/distinctive term appears verbatim in the corpus), conceptual (paraphrased idea, some vocabulary overlap possible), cross_vocabulary (deliberately different wording, minimal token overlap with the target), ambiguous_control (a query where superficially-AI-related corpus items exist but are NOT a strong direct answer — tests over-claiming), filtered (combined with a real source/time/bookmark filter).

rubric.2: directly relevant / strong search result for this specific query
rubric.1: partially relevant / useful but indirect, broad, or secondary
rubric.0: not useful for this query, even if generally related to AI

queries.expectedRationale: Exact repo name in corpus (github:937253475) — a direct hit should score 2; anything else is at best 1.
Exact repo Significant-Gravitas/AutoGPT exists (github:614765452) — the one clear 2.
Exact repo tensorflow/tensorflow exists (github:45717250), a common single word — tests whether lexical's exact match beats semantic's broader ML-adjacent noise.
Exact repo browser-use/browser-use exists (github:881458615).
Exact paper title/acronym exists (arxiv:2609.11582) — a rare, distinctive token; any method missing this on an exact-acronym query has a real gap.
Literal phrase in arxiv:2609.11550's title — a direct 2; unrelated ML papers should not outrank it.
Literal phrase in arxiv:2609.11601 (MMGait) title.
Literal phrase in arxiv:2609.11569 (EXYGEN) — 'knowledge graph (KG) understanding'.

Literal term in arxiv:2609.11532 (Prompt Revision as a Source of Cultural Bias in Text-to-Image Systems) — should NOT be satisfied by the unrelated text-to-speech paper (arxiv:2609.11545), a useful lexical-precision check.

queries.query: reducing memory usage when AI models process audio and video together
queries.expectedRationale: Paraphrase of arxiv:2609.11582 (OmniKVQuant: 'Omni-modal LLMs take in audio, video and text... KV cache memory cost grows'), with real but partial vocabulary overlap ('memory', 'audio', 'video').

queries.query: using AI to search for new antibiotics
queries.expectedRationale: Paraphrase of the OpenAI RSS item (id 105): 'search living and extinct genomes for antimicrobial candidates to fight drug-resistant infections' — 'antibiotics' vs 'antimicrobial' is a real but mild vocabulary gap.

queries.query: predicting how severe a car crash will be
queries.expectedRationale: Paraphrase of arxiv:2609.11592 (crash-severity prediction certification framework).

queries.query: AI that helps forecast a company's financial performance using alternative data sources
queries.expectedRationale: Close paraphrase of arxiv:2609.11607 (Making Alternative Data Work: Context-Augmented LLMs for Financial Forecasting) — high vocabulary overlap, borderline conceptual/literal.

queries.query: software that watches your bank transactions to guess how a business is doing
queries.expectedRationale: Heavy paraphrase of arxiv:2609.11607, deliberately avoiding 'alternative data'/'forecasting'/'financial' tokens.

queries.query: AI that can click around a website by itself
queries.expectedRationale: Cross-vocabulary phrasing of github:881458615's own description ('Agents that use the browser') — avoids 'browser', 'agent', 'automation' tokens entirely.

queries.query: computer vision for spotting early-stage cancer
queries.expectedRationale: Cross-vocabulary phrasing of arxiv:2609.11550 (melanoma/CNN detection) — avoids 'melanoma', 'skin', 'CNN' entirely; 'cancer' and 'computer vision' are the only bridges.

queries.query: shrinking large language models so they run on cheaper hardware
queries.expectedRationale: Plausible but indirect link to arxiv:2609.11582 (KV cache quantization reduces runtime memory, not model size/weights) — a defensible EXPECTATION IS A 1, NOT A 2: this deliberately tests whether a method over-credits a topically-close-but-not-quite-right paper with full relevance.

No corpus item is actually about AGI timeline forecasting. GPT-6 Astra (a product launch) and 'The AI policy window is open' (policy essay) are the closest AI-adjacent items but are NOT direct answers — the defensible expectation is that nothing scores above 1, and anything scored 2 here is a strong signal of over-claiming relevance purely from topical proximity.

arxiv:2609.11527 (LiDAR cone detection for Formula Student Driverless) is about autonomous-vehicle PERCEPTION, not safety REGULATIONS — topically adjacent (autonomous vehicles) but not a direct answer to a regulatory question. Defensible ceiling: 1, not 2.

The corpus's closest items are 'Introducing ChatGPT for Financial Services' (a specific vertical, not general customer service) and GPT-Live-1 (a voice API, not a customer-service product). Neither is a direct match — tests whether a method returns these as strong ('2') hits purely because they mention chat/voice/AI.

queries.query: using AI to write video game code
queries.expectedRationale: Corpus has general coding-agent repos (claude-code, AutoGPT) and a game-AI research post ('From Atari to EVE Online' — AI PLAYING games, not writing game code) — neither directly answers 'AI that writes game code'. Defensible ceiling: 1.
Literal phrase in the OpenAI RSS item (id 122): 'GPT-5.6 Sol helps run quantum computing experiments' — a clean, distinctive exact-phrase target for lexical.

queries.query: AI model that predicts the weather
queries.expectedRationale: Paraphrase of 'WeatherNext 3' (id 132) and possibly TimesFM-3 (id 144, general forecasting, weaker fit) — tests whether a method correctly ranks the direct weather-model hit above the more general time-series-forecasting one.
Many github items are literally agent frameworks/repos (AutoGPT, langchain, dify, browser-use, hermes-agent, etc.) — a broad-recall filtered check, not a single-target one.

Several HN items directly reference OpenAI (hn:49649213 'OpenAI Agents API', hn:49650326 'OpenAI's Navier-Stokes release', hn:49639408 'trust OpenAI with unpublished math') — checks the sourceType filter holds and lexical/semantic both surface the obviously-relevant HN threads over the less-relevant ones (e.g. the Thelio Mira hardware post, which does not mention OpenAI).

Exactly one item is bookmarked in this dev corpus (anthropics/claude-code, bookmarked specifically for this benchmark). A correct implementation returns exactly that one item across all three methods; anything else returned (or the bookmarked item omitted) is a filter defect, not a relevance judgment call.
